title: Cloudflare global WAF CPU exhaustion
source_title: Details of the Cloudflare outage on July 2, 2019
alert: Public reports show widespread 502 errors shortly after a firewall rule update. Investigate which functions were affected, the documented cause, and the response decision.

evidence.text: A WAF Managed Rules update was deployed at 13:42 UTC; it included a regular expression with severe backtracking behavior.
External WAF checks and other end-to-end checks began failing; widespread 502 responses and high CPU were observed.
Investigators identified the WAF as the source, ruling out an attack; CPU and tracing information pointed to rule execution.
An emergency global WAF termination was executed; by 14:09 traffic and CPU had returned to expected levels.
After local positive and negative tests confirmed the fix, WAF functionality was re-enabled globally.
The postmortem identified insufficient regex complexity safeguards, no performance test, an overly broad rollout, and slow recovery access paths.
The outage affected Cloudflare core proxying, CDN and WAF functionality worldwide.

root_hypotheses.description: A WAF regex with catastrophic backtracking exhausted CPU during global rollout
A hardware power interruption at the origin data center
A DDoS attack saturated the public edge

response_options.description: Globally disable the affected WAF component/rule and validate rollback, then restore protection after testing
Increase DNS TTL for all zones
Force every customer to change origin endpoints
Keep the problematic rule running while adding more proxy workers

dataset_origin: Published first-party incident postmortem; curated and paraphrased source facts (NOT original telemetry)
